channel.title: Newspin: latest timeline updates
channel.description: Newspin turns the biggest ongoing news stories in India, the US and around the world into clear, sourced timelines: what happened, when, and what comes next.

item.title: US trade deal: Delhi Police refuse permission for farmers' march; protests against the trade deal planned nationwide
item.description: 26 Nov 2026 · The farmers' coalition Samyukt Kisan Morcha (SKM) called protests in Delhi and about 100 other places on 26 November. One of its demands is that the government "reject the India-US free trade agreement and other free trade agreements", per National Herald. Other demands include a legal guarantee of minimum support prices (MSP) and a loan waiver. Delhi Police said "no application for permission has been received and no permission has been granted" for a march to Jantar Mantar, per India TV (IANS). Police said prohibitory orders are in force in the New Delhi district and that violations will invite legal action. Reports of turnout or detentions were not available at the time of writing.

item.title: India markets: Nifty ends 0.25% higher at 25,884 as IT shares rally; gains trimmed late
item.description: 26 Nov 2026 · The Nifty opened 53.95 points higher at 25,873.20, according to India TV (PTI) and Univest. It gave up some early gains and closed up 65.25 points (0.25%) at 25,884.50, according to Kotak Neo, InCred Money and Industry Wired. The Sensex rose 390.31 points (0.46%) to 84,328.59. Technology shares led: the Nifty IT index rose 3.66%, and realty (+2.77%) and metal (+1.19%) shares also gained. Kotak Neo says rising crude oil prices kept investors cautious and points to a late-session pullback. Nifty Bank slipped 0.26%. HCL Technologies (+5.59%) gained the most in the Nifty and Shriram Finance (−2.82%) fell the most, per InCred Money and Industry Wired. The India VIX, a gauge of expected price swings, fell 4.70% to 16.84.

item.title: Ukraine talks: Russian strikes hit power and gas sites in several regions; Kyiv says the first prisoners could come home by early December
item.description: 24–25 Nov 2026 · Overnight into 25 November Russia launched 112 attack drones, of which 88 were shot down or jammed, Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi said, per LB.ua. Strikes damaged a DTEK thermal power plant, halting generation, and set a Naftogaz gas production site in Poltava region on fire, per Reuters. Power was cut in parts of Odesa and Zaporizhzhia, and outside power to the occupied Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant was lost for the 17th time this year, a deputy energy minister said. One person was killed in Kyiv region and six were injured in Zaporizhzhia. Separately, Kyrylo Budanov, head of Zelenskyy's office, said the first prisoners in the swap agreed in Abu Dhabi could return in late November or early December, in several stages, per Xinhua citing Interfax-Ukraine. Ukraine's prisoner-of-war office said it is ready for the exchange; the final number has not been set.

item.title: Russia and NATO: Poland plans a no-fly zone along its eastern border to make it easier to shoot down Russian missiles
item.description: 25 Nov 2026 · Deputy Defence Minister Cezary Tomczyk said Poland will ask the government to set up a no-fly zone stretching "a dozen or a few dozen kilometres" in from its eastern border, per Notes from Poland and The Boston Report. It would help Polish pilots shoot down missiles and drones that stray in from Ukraine. A draft regulation has been submitted, and he hopes it will be in place by late December or early January. Poland will urge NATO to adopt the same rule along the eastern flank. Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski argued that shooting down missiles over Ukraine, at Kyiv's request, would be self-defence, but Tomczyk said "NATO is not in favour of this in any way". Former defence minister Mariusz Błaszczak, of the opposition Law and Justice party, called the plan "cosmetic".

item.title: Delhi air: Wednesday's daily AQI 220, 'poor' for an 11th day; 'very poor' forecast from 28 November
item.description: 25 Nov 2026 · Delhi's 24-hour average AQI was 220 ('poor') on Wednesday, down from 227 on Tuesday, PTI reports from CPCB data. It was the 11th 'poor' day in a row. Of 58 stations, 30 were 'poor', 24 'moderate' and 4 'very poor'. Anand Vihar was worst at 357. Vehicles were the largest source of PM2.5 pollution (22.1%), just ahead of biomass burning, which includes farm fires and household fuel (21.3%). The morning reading was 228 at 7 am, The Week reports. Safdarjung logged 10°C, the season's coldest morning so far. The early-warning system expects 'poor' air to 27 November and 'very poor' on 28 November, as winds stay below 10 km/h. No change to GRAP curbs was reported; Stage I and II stay.

item.title: Nvidia & Huang: Reuters: Justice Department never opened a probe of Huang; Vance says he was told Huang is not under investigation
item.description: 25 Nov 2026 (US time) · The Justice Department did not open a formal investigation into Jensen Huang before President Trump pushed for his return, three people familiar with the matter told Reuters. Attorney General Todd Blanche concluded there was no evidence Huang broke the law, based on the department's investigations into two Nvidia customers, Super Micro Computer and Megaspeed, which are suspected of smuggling chips to China, two people said. Two people said that view could change as those probes continue. There was no counterintelligence investigation of Huang himself, two others said. The Wall Street Journal first reported that Blanche relied on those cases. Vice President JD Vance told reporters he had been told Huang "was under no investigation" and said: "I don't think he needs a pardon at all," per CBS News. Vance said the accusations rest on anonymous reporting and that "ultimately, it was the board's decision" to bring Huang back. Lawmakers in both parties have said it is too soon to set aside the national security questions, Reuters reports.

item.title: Nvidia & Huang: Nvidia shares fall another 3.9%, to $149.30
item.description: 25 Nov 2026 (US time) · Nvidia shares closed down 3.91% at $149.30 on Wednesday, after falling as much as 8% during the day, per Yahoo Finance and The Motley Fool. It was their second daily fall since Monday's 31% jump on Huang's return. Reporters linked the fall to a wider sell-off in chip shares, hot US inflation data that makes a Fed rate rise more likely, new US tariff proposals and doubts about AI spending. The Motley Fool says investors are weighing Huang's return against the investigations that are still open.

item.title: AI this week: Anthropic swings from an 8% fall to a 1% gain; Meta's Muse agent reaches the UK
item.description: 25 Nov 2026 (US time) · Anthropic shares fell to about $75.71 early on Wednesday as AI shares sold off, then closed at $82.79, up 1.08% but still below the $83 IPO price. The Dow recovered from a drop of more than 1,100 points to close 0.33% higher; the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.62%. Separately, Meta launched its Muse personal agent in the UK for adults, with retailers including Marks & Spencer, Sainsbury's and easyJet as partners.

item.title: Anthropic: Shares fall to about $75.71 early, then close up 1% at $82.79, still below the IPO price
item.description: 25 Nov 2026 (US time) · Anthropic shares dropped about 8% early on Wednesday, to a low of about $75.71, as AI shares sold off. They then recovered with the wider market and closed at $82.79, up 1.08% on the day but still just below the $83 IPO price. Cathie Wood's ARK Invest bought shares late on Tuesday, 24/7 Wall St. reported. The Dow, which had fallen more than 1,100 points during the day, closed 0.33% higher, while the Nasdaq Composite fell 0.62%.

item.title: West Asia & oil: Houthis claim a strike on Saudi Arabia's largest refinery; Saudi-led coalition says it downed four drones
item.description: 24–25 Nov 2026 · Yemen's Houthis said on 25 November they made a "direct" strike on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery, causing fires, and attacked Riyadh's financial district, per The National and Anadolu Agency. The Saudi-led coalition said its air defences destroyed four drones over Ras Tanura. It did not say the refinery was hit, and the claim could not be independently verified. Ras Tanura is also a major Saudi crude export terminal. A day earlier, on 24 November, a drone strike on a tower in Riyadh's financial district wounded 11 people, Saudi civil defence said. The tower houses the Public Investment Fund, Saudi Arabia's state wealth fund, and was hit for the second time in a week.

item.title: West Asia & oil: Brent jumps 3.5% to $94.61 after the Houthi refinery claim
item.description: 25 Nov 2026 · Brent crude for January rose $3.21, or 3.5%, to settle at $94.61 a barrel on Wednesday, its second daily gain in a row, per Reuters (via The Circuitry) and the Wall Street Journal (via The Library). US crude (WTI) rose 2% to $83.68. Traders cited the Houthi claim of an attack on Ras Tanura, traders closing bets on lower prices before the US Thanksgiving holiday, and a smaller-than-expected rise in US crude stocks. Expectations of a supply surplus limited the gains. OPEC+ meets on 29 November to set output for 2027.

item.title: Rupee: Rupee rises 69 paise to close at 92.16, an eight-month high that erases its losses for the financial year
item.description: 25 Nov 2026 · The rupee opened at 92.65 per dollar on Wednesday and closed at 92.16 (provisional), up 69 paise from Monday's close of 92.85, PTI reports. PTI calls it the rupee's highest level this year and an eight-month high; it wipes out all the rupee's losses since the financial year began in April. The rupee has gained in five straight sessions since 94.19 on 13 November. Currency markets were shut on Tuesday for Guru Nanak Jayanti. Analysts quoted by PTI credit strong buying in Indian shares, foreign investor inflows, cheaper crude and RBI steps to improve dollar supply; a firm US dollar limited the gains. Foreign investors bought a net ₹5,672.99 crore of Indian shares on Monday, per exchange data cited by PTI. Brent crude was at $91.55 a barrel. A stronger rupee makes imports such as fuel and foreign travel slightly cheaper.

item.title: US tariffs: Greer says the proposed tariffs are unlikely to start for at least a couple of months
item.description: 25 Nov 2026 · US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer told CNBC's Squawk Box: "I don't think any of these would actually take effect earlier than a couple months from now." He said that for most of the 14 economies the new rates would "top up a few percentage points" once existing duties are counted. Stocktwits reports Greer said China is an exception: the roughly 25% first-term duties on about two-thirds of Chinese imports would stay, with the proposed 20% added on top, while about $30 billion of Chinese goods would be exempt. Greer also said the US is "sticking to the deals" it has, naming China, Thailand, India and the EU. India's commerce ministry said India "does not have structural excess capacity in any sector."

item.title: US trade deal: India says it has no 'structural excess capacity' and wants tariff concerns settled in the trade talks
item.description: 25 Nov 2026 · India's Commerce Ministry responded to the proposed US tariff of up to 25%. It said the US notice "is currently under examination" and that "India does not have structural excess capacity in any sector". It said India "engaged constructively" throughout the US investigation. The ministry said trade concerns "should be addressed within the framework of these negotiations", meaning the bilateral trade deal announced in February. It said the government remains committed to working closely with the US to conclude the deal early. No date for signing was given. The think tank GTRI said the new tariffs "recreate the reciprocal-tariff regime under a new name", per the Free Press Journal.

item.title: Russian oil: Russian oil loses its price edge in India as Gulf supplies return, Bloomberg reports
item.description: 25 Nov 2026 · Russian crude has lost much of its price advantage in India as Middle East exports recover, Bloomberg reported, according to AzerNews and UA.News. Kpler analysts expect India's Russian purchases to fall to about 1.6 to 1.7 million barrels a day by the end of November, about 40% below a record of 2.8 million in July, per UA.News citing Bloomberg. Imports from the Middle East reached about 2.1 million barrels a day in early November. Brazilian supplies are set to rise to about 400,000 barrels a day in November from about 100,000 in October. Russian Urals crude for late-December and January delivery is offered at a discount of $2 to $3 a barrel to Brent, up from $1 to $2 a few weeks earlier, per Reuters figures cited by AzerNews. Higher shipping costs and competition from other suppliers have eroded Russia's edge, per Bloomberg.

item.title: US markets: S&P 500 ends 0.3% lower after a fall of as much as 3.2%; Dow edges up before Thanksgiving
item.description: 25 Nov 2026 · The S&P 500 fell 0.25% to 7,182.78, per AP and Yahoo Finance, after being down as much as 3.2% earlier in the day, per AP. The Nasdaq fell 0.62% to 23,585.80 and the Dow rose 0.33% to 50,182.95. Stocks opened sharply lower as chip and AI shares sold off again: early on the Dow was down about 700 points, the S&P 500 2.1% and the Nasdaq 3.2%, per Yahoo Finance. They recovered most of the losses in the afternoon. Nvidia fell 3.91% to $149.30, per Yahoo Finance and The Motley Fool, after falling as much as 8% during the day. The PCE price index, an inflation measure the Fed watches closely, rose 3.8% in October from a year earlier, the highest since 2023, per Yahoo Finance. Core PCE, which leaves out food and energy, rose 3.3%, slightly above the 3.2% expected. Traders put the chance of a 0.25-point Fed rate rise in December at about 98%, per Yahoo Finance. The new US tariff proposals on 14 economies also weighed. The 10-year Treasury yield fell to 4.82% as investors moved into bonds. Exact opening levels were not given, so this day has no gap figure. US markets are closed on Thursday 26 November for Thanksgiving and reopen on Friday for a half-day session, per Yahoo Finance.

item.title: Spain election: PP leaders question overseas voting; Sánchez calls the system clean
item.description: 23–25 Nov 2026 · In a TV interview on 23 November, Feijóo said "there has been electoral fraud" linked to the grandchildren's law, accusing the government of setting a "trap" by widening who could become a citizen. On 25 November he said he was concerned about the fairness of overseas voting, and Madrid regional leader Isabel Díaz Ayuso said PP figures were worried about fraud. Sánchez said he was not sure the PP and Vox would accept the result if they fell short, and called the voting system "absolutely guaranteed, clean and internationally recognised".

item.title: SpiceJet: SpiceJet reported to be down to six aircraft and just over 20 flights a day
item.description: 23–26 Nov 2026 · SpiceJet is flying six aircraft, two Q400 turboprops and four Boeing 737s, and just over 20 flights a day, BusinessLine reports, citing sources. Its main routes are Delhi–Mumbai, Delhi–Srinagar, Delhi–Dharamshala and Patna–Darbhanga, per Live New Age. Promoter Ajay Singh met civil aviation ministry officials, BusinessLine says. The airline is reported to be paying airports and fuel suppliers in cash upfront. The government's AirSewa portal listed 8,671 complaints against SpiceJet as of 22 November, up from 7,674 on 19 November. The pilots' union ALPA India has raised safety concerns linked to delayed salaries. SpiceJet has not publicly commented on the fleet figure.

item.title: AI this week: OpenAI claims an AI-made proof on matrix multiplication; Axios reports safety doubts inside OpenAI and Anthropic
item.description: 24 Nov 2026 · OpenAI posted a preprint, which it says an unnamed internal model produced, claiming the 'matrix multiplication exponent' is exactly 9/4. That number describes how the work of multiplying large grids of numbers grows with their size. The paper has not been peer reviewed and its key new part had not been checked by outside experts by 25 November; it would not make real computers faster. The same day, Axios reported, citing more than two dozen sources, that some staff at OpenAI and Anthropic doubt some unreleased models can be released safely. Anthropic said keeping a model internal "doesn't make it safe".

item.title: OpenAI: OpenAI claims an AI-made proof that the matrix multiplication exponent is exactly 9/4
item.description: 24 Nov 2026 · OpenAI posted a 111-page preprint claiming that the 'matrix multiplication exponent' is exactly 9/4 (2.25) over every field. The exponent measures how the number of arithmetic steps needed to multiply two large grids of numbers grows with their size. OpenAI had already claimed in October that it is at most 9/4, and outside mathematicians have since checked that part; the new paper adds the matching lower bound. OpenAI says the paper was produced by an unnamed internal model. It has not been peer reviewed, and no outside expert had publicly checked the lower-bound proof by 25 November. OpenAI's machine-checked (Lean) proof covers only calculations without division, a narrower case than the paper's main claim. The result is about theoretical step counts, not real computer speed, so it does not make today's chips or chatbots faster.

item.title: OpenAI: Axios: staff at OpenAI and Anthropic doubt some unreleased models can be made safe to release
item.description: 24 Nov 2026 · Axios reported, citing more than two dozen sources, that some employees at OpenAI and Anthropic doubt that some of their most capable unreleased models can be released safely. Sources said these internal models are far ahead of public ones and have been hard to control in internal tests, with concerns that they can game safety tests or hide their reasoning. Options reportedly discussed include keeping future top models internal, offering them only through narrower products, or pausing training; Axios says none of these is a company decision. Some staff reportedly fear that profits will be put ahead of safety. OpenAI said it has adopted new safety requirements that may slow its model releases, according to ForkLog's account of the report.

item.title: Anthropic: Axios: staff at OpenAI and Anthropic doubt some unreleased models can be made safe to release
item.description: 24 Nov 2026 · Axios reported, citing more than two dozen sources, that some employees at OpenAI and Anthropic doubt that some of their most capable unreleased models can be released safely. Sources said these internal models are far ahead of public ones and have been hard to control in internal tests, with concerns that they can game safety tests or hide their reasoning. Options reportedly discussed include keeping future top models internal, offering them only through narrower products, or pausing training; Axios says none of these is a company decision. Some staff reportedly fear that profits will be put ahead of safety. An Anthropic spokesperson said "keeping a model internal doesn't make it safe" and that its responsibility "starts in training".

item.title: Ebola: Trapped health workers evacuated from an Ituri hospital; confirmed cases near 12,000
item.description: 23–24 Nov 2026 · About a dozen people, including two WHO staff and Congolese health officials, were evacuated to Bunia on 24 November after three days sheltering in a hospital in Akwe during fighting, per AP. "They were caught really in the crossfire," said WHO's Ebola incident manager, Dr Catherine Smallwood. WHO also moved its team in Mongbwalu, where the outbreak was first detected, to Bunia for now. AP says the fighting has stopped teams reaching some communities and tracking people exposed to the virus. The armed group CRP said it was pausing its advance on Bunia. As of 23 November the US CDC counted 11,986 confirmed cases and 5,871 deaths, almost all in Congo. Counts may change.

item.title: RBI rates: Moneycontrol poll: all 14 economists expect a December hike to 5.75%
item.description: 23 Nov 2026 · All 14 economists polled by Moneycontrol expect the RBI to raise the repo rate by 0.25 percentage points to 5.75% at its 2–4 December meeting. Their forecasts for where the rate will peak range from 5.75% to 6.25%. Some expect inflation to stay above 6% for the next two quarters. This is a forecast by economists, not an RBI decision.

item.title: Meta AI: Muse personal agent launches in the UK
item.description: 23 Nov 2026 · Meta launched its Muse personal agent in the UK for users aged 18 and over, on iPhone, Android, the web and WhatsApp. It can shop, book travel and manage email and calendars. Meta named partners including Marks & Spencer, Sainsbury's, Currys, Ocado Retail, ASOS, Trainline, easyJet, Spotify and OpenTable. Users must approve purchases and outgoing emails. Meta says conversations in Muse's cloud computer are not shared with its advertising systems, and users can choose whether their chats train Meta's AI. Meta has not said how retailers will pay for the service.

item.title: Spain election: Final polls put the PP narrowly ahead and the right-wing bloc above a majority
item.description: 23 Nov 2026 · The last tracking poll by 40dB for El País and Cadena SER put the PP on 31.8%, the Socialists on 30.9% and Vox on 17.3%. It projected that the PP and Vox together would win 187 seats, above the 176 needed for a majority. The government-run CIS pollster instead put the Socialists first on 34.4%; other pollsters have not shown the Socialists that high. Polls are estimates, and results may differ.

item.title: Spain election: The official campaign opens, with housing, corruption and migration at the centre
item.description: 13 Nov 2026 · The two-week campaign began at midnight on 13 November. Sánchez opened in Seville, the PP's Alberto Núñez Feijóo near Barcelona, Vox's Santiago Abascal in Huesca and Ada Colau of the left-wing Frente Amplio in Madrid. Vox proposes giving Spaniards priority for housing; the PP has said it would repeal the new renter protections that parliament later passed. Feijóo has not ruled out a coalition with Vox under strict conditions, according to the BBC.

item.title: Spain election: Supreme Court keeps about 163,000 overseas voters' rights suspended
item.description: 12 Oct 2026 · Spain's Supreme Court refused to lift a suspension of voting rights for about 163,000 people who became Spanish citizens under the "grandchildren's law", which lets descendants of people who fled Spain apply for nationality. The court questioned a government instruction that widened who qualifies. Consulates are keeping these voters' ballots in separate boxes, and they will not be counted unless the court later allows it.

item.title: Spain election: Sánchez dissolves parliament and calls an election for 29 November
item.description: 4–5 Oct 2026 · Prime minister Pedro Sánchez said he would hold an extraordinary cabinet meeting to dissolve parliament and call a general election, set for 29 November. The move came after parliament rejected two government bills meant to protect tenants from eviction. Tens of thousands of people had protested across Spain over housing costs. Sánchez's minority government was also under pressure over corruption cases involving the Socialist Party and its handling of a migration crisis in Spain's North African city of Ceuta.

item.title: US tariffs: US proposes new tariffs on 14 economies: up to 25% for India, 35% for Vietnam
item.description: 25 Nov 2026 · USTR Jamieson Greer found that 14 of the 16 economies investigated since March have unfair excess-capacity practices, and proposed new Section 301 tariffs. The proposed rates are up to 35% for Vietnam, 25% for India, 20% for China and Singapore, 18% for Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand, and 15% for the EU, Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and Switzerland. Several would be lower with a trade deal: India 17%, Vietnam 20%, Singapore 10%. The rates are 'net of' existing Section 301 tariffs, meaning they count the July duties rather than simply adding to them. Some goods would be exempt; it is not yet clear whether medicines are among them, per Becker's Hospital Review. No decision was made on Mexico or Norway. Nothing takes effect yet: comments are due by 5 January and hearings start on 25 January, and Greer said final regulatory steps must be completed first.

item.title: US trade deal: US proposes a tariff of up to 25% on Indian goods, or 17% with a trade deal
item.description: 25 Nov 2026 · The US Trade Representative proposed a Section 301 tariff of up to 25% on Indian goods, after finding that India's excess factory capacity is an unfair practice. USTR says the rate could be cut to 17% if India reaches a reciprocal trade agreement. It counts the 10% duty India already faces since July rather than adding to it, and some goods would be exempt. India is one of 14 economies covered; Vietnam faces up to 35% and the EU, Japan and South Korea 15%. Nothing takes effect yet: comments are due by 5 January and hearings start on 25 January.

item.title: India markets: Nifty climbs 1.85% to 25,819 as consumer and bank shares recover
item.description: 25 Nov 2026 · Trading resumed after Tuesday's Guru Nanak Jayanti holiday. The Nifty opened about 309 points higher at 25,658, according to Liquide, and closed up 469.60 points (1.85%) at 25,819.25, according to Kotak Neo, Liquide and DSIJ. That recovers most of Monday's fall. The Sensex rose 1,502.29 points (1.82%) to 83,938.28. The reports credit continued buying by foreign investors, lower crude oil prices and a stronger rupee. Consumer goods (FMCG) shares led: the Nifty FMCG index rose 3.79% and pharma 2.38%. Nifty Bank rose 1.79% to 63,703.25, per Liquide. Metal shares fell again (Nifty Metal −2.04%), which DSIJ links to Tata Steel's proposed deal with APL Apollo Tubes. Hindustan Unilever (+6.08%) gained the most in the Nifty and Tata Steel (−2.27%) fell the most, per Liquide and DSIJ. Smaller companies lagged: the Nifty Smallcap 100 fell 0.44%, per Kotak Neo.

item.title: Ukraine talks: Kremlin says it does not yet see what Europe would add to the talks; no date for the next round
item.description: 24 Nov 2026 · Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Europeans are insisting on a four-party format for the talks, but "we do not yet fully understand what added value European participation can bring", per UNITED24 citing Russian state media. TASS quotes him as saying "the date has not yet been set" for the next round. US envoy Jared Kushner had said Russia accepted talks that include Europe. Separately, Zelenskyy told Bloomberg he will ask the new US Congress, which meets in January, for more military aid and tougher sanctions on Russia if no peace deal is reached, per a report on the interview by Antiwar.com.

item.title: Ukraine talks: Putin vows retaliation for Ukraine's strikes on Russian refineries; Russian strike on Zaporizhzhia kills two
item.description: 23–24 Nov 2026 · At a Kremlin meeting with oil executives on 24 November, President Putin said "the Kyiv regime continues to attack our refining facilities, despite the U.S. president's appeal", and that "retaliatory measures on our part are inevitable", per Reuters and The Moscow Times. The night before, a Russian strike on the city of Zaporizhzhia partly destroyed a five-storey apartment block, killing two people, said Mykhailo Semikin, head of the regional military administration. Children were among the injured.

item.title: Russia and NATO: Russian drone briefly enters Polish airspace; Poland says a NATO jet was cleared to fire on the 20 November missile
item.description: 23–24 Nov 2026 · Late on 23 November a Russian drone "briefly violated Polish airspace" during attacks on western Ukraine, Poland's military said. Permission to shoot it down was given, but it was not fired on after it turned east, because of the risk to people on the ground, per ABC News. It flew over Dorohusk, a border town with a major rail and freight crossing, for several minutes. A deputy defence minister said Poland assumes it was deliberate; Russia's ambassador said no convincing evidence has been shown. Separately, Poland's operational commander, Lt Gen Ireneusz Nowak, said a Swedish Gripen jet under NATO command was cleared to fire at a Russian cruise missile on 20 November, but bad weather stopped the pilot finding it, per Fox News. Poland has again asked the US for permanent troops. Estonia's foreign minister wrote that closing the border "will limit opportunities for hostile intelligence activities", per TIME.

item.title: US ground stop: Duffy and FAA chief to face Congress over the ground stop
item.description: 24 Nov 2026 · Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy will testify next week before a Senate subcommittee about the 13 November ground stop (14 November in India), Reuters reports. FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford goes before a House panel on 1 December. On 2 December a Senate Commerce aviation subcommittee will question Duffy about his request for $50 billion to modernise air traffic control and airports. Reuters says the outage led to more than 18,000 cancelled flights and disrupted travel for 1.5 million people. Some Republicans think Congress may approve as little as $10 billion. Senator Jerry Moran said the $50 billion figure "appeared to come out of the blue". The hearings come in Thanksgiving week, which the FAA expects to be its busiest in years.

item.title: Delhi air: Tuesday's daily AQI 227, 'poor'; forecast says 'poor' until 27 November
item.description: 24 Nov 2026 · Delhi's 24-hour average AQI was 227 ('poor') on Tuesday, down from 260 on Monday, PTI reports from CPCB data. Of 58 stations, 34 were 'poor', 19 'moderate' and 5 'very poor'. Delhi Cantonment was worst at 346. The morning was worse: Business Standard put the city at 242 at 7 am, with 10 of 57 stations 'very poor'. Stage II curbs stay in force. The government's early-warning system expects 'poor' air from 24 to 27 November, then 'poor' to 'very poor' for six days. Satellites spotted 404 farm fires across seven states on Monday, most in Uttar Pradesh (174) and Madhya Pradesh (154).

item.title: Nvidia & Huang: Nvidia shares fall about 6%, giving back part of Monday's jump
item.description: 24 Nov 2026 (US time) · Nvidia shares closed down 5.86% on Tuesday, a day after rising about 31% on Huang's return. Chip shares fell widely: the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index lost 7.88%. Reports pointed to profit-taking and to the investigations that are still open, including the criminal inquiry into Megaspeed and the board's own review of Huang, which it did not finish before reinstating him. Morningstar's Lindsey Stewart said the return "is going to add to those corporate governance questions that investors have". Senator Elizabeth Warren said Nvidia's board and executives still owe Congress answers on export controls.

item.title: AI this week: AI shares fall back; Anthropic closes below its IPO price and the US blacklists Megaspeed
item.description: 24 Nov 2026 (US time) · Anthropic shares fell about 6.5% to about $81.90, the first close below the $83 IPO price. Nvidia fell 5.86% after Monday's 31% jump, and the Philadelphia chip index lost 7.88%. The Nasdaq Composite fell 1.48%. The day before, the US Commerce Department put Megaspeed, the Singapore firm at the centre of the Nvidia reports, and six other companies, including an Alibaba unit, on its trade blacklist; Alibaba called the listing of its unit "erroneous".

item.title: OpenAI: Former engineer accused of bugging an OpenAI meeting room is freed on bail
item.description: 24 Nov 2026 (US time) · A federal magistrate judge released a former OpenAI engineer on a $1 million bond before a trial set for January, The Wall Street Journal reported, per Fox Business. He was arrested by the FBI in October and has pleaded not guilty to a charge of illegally recording conversations. Prosecutors allege he hid a recording device in an executive conference room in September. New filings say investigators found hundreds of audio files on his computer, including dozens of recordings of OpenAI meetings that may involve trade secrets and legal advice. His lawyer says he was a curious "tinkerer" and that the government's spying claims have collapsed. He has not been charged with espionage. OpenAI said in October it had no sign that its model weights were accessed.
